title: Dead Rising 2: Off the Record
text: Should you buy this or Dead Rising 2? well here are a few of the differences between the two: -In OTR you don't have to run back to the safehouse to give your daughter zombrex, since you don't have one. Instead you give it to yourself at any place on the map. -You're Frank West, he has more personality than Chuck Greene and he has a camera which you can use to help level up. -Bosses in OTR have damage peaks meaning that you can't just keep wailing away at a boss and have them die quickly. The damage you do now goes down by half every hit after the first one. -More combo weapons and a new area "Uranus Zone" also 2 new bosses which are pretty cool. -The story is different, especially around the end of the game. -Looking at your watch now pauses the game which it didn't do in DR2, and the map is on the same screen as your watch and you can now set waypoints, which makes things more convenient. -Money has more of a purpose now, not going to spoil why, but grab as much as you can! Other stuff to note: -From my experience, controllers do not work with OTR. -Runs good even on max settings. -Some people can't get co-op to work but I have never tried it so do some research on it if you plan on playing with a friend. Overall: great game, I would give it a 9/10

title: Dead Rising 2: Off the Record
text: I really don't find this any worse or any better than Dead Rising 2. If anything, buy this AND Dead Rising 2 (if you can). Dead Rising 2 is the canon one, so just play that first and then this. What makes Dead Rising 2: OTR a worthy recommendation, however, is, well, Frank West. He adds just that right amount of sass to every bit of story that makes it a little more enjoyable than mr. perfect scowly-face Chuck (who is a psycho in this one). There are more combo weapons, a new area to explore, a different narrative (that hits most of the same beats, but every cutscene has been redone for Frank and his dry humour), a SANDBOX MODE (which we had been clamoring for since the bonus of infinite mode in Dead Rising 1 was not present in 2), new Psychos, and the return of Frank's camera. With the return of photos is the ability to snap selfies with zombies (which, somehow, kills them... which is glorious). Overall, it's a worthy purchase. As worthy as Dead Rising 2.

title: DeadCore
text: Seeing how many people compare this game to portal let me explain why that isnt really possible and then I talk about my opinion on deadcore itself. Deadcore is a game about reflexes/physical challenges in general. You know what you have to do, but good luck pulling it off. Sometimes you can improve your performance by figuring out an even faster way to nmove on and sometimes finding collectibles requires some thinking but you can play through without ever just standing there for half an hour wondering what to do next.  Portal on the other hand is figuring out the solution to a puzzle. Actually performing that solution in most cases isnt that hard. Secondly there is nigh 0 story in Deadcore. That is not a bad thing, it isnt neccesary. There are hidden collectibles that give access to texts that will give you an idea of what the story is, but you have to find those first, so there is a good chance you go through the game without any story, also there is no voiceacting. This of course also means that there is no humor, but again that is not what this game is about or needs. Meanwhile Portal has its great and funny voiceactors that carry you through the game and you always know why you are where you are etc. third the gun. yeah you use a physics doing gun in each game. In deadcore it is used to disable enemies and activate or deactive different mechanics, you dont always need it, there is a good chance you can get through a section without using your gun once. In Portal it basically is your main mechanic So yeah that should explain why its an apple-pears comparison. Now deadcore itself in my opinion was great fun. Some say it is to difficult and I can agree that it can get punishingly tough, but the last checkpoint usually wasnt far away and you get right back in the action. Id say a downside is falling off stuff since you are basically waiting to slam into death or going to the menu and clicking restart from checkpoint, neither of which are as fast as dying from anything else. The abilitys all work and except for a rocket-jump like function all work very well, though sometimes precise landing can be a problem when for example your dash shoots you farther than you wanted. The rocket-jumpish ability btw almost never comes into use (in my playstyle, which means just trying to finish the level) so it isnt a problem. Now the mechanics of the game world itself are mostly pretty good, but the gravitation changing combined with your camera moving and often the gravitation sections being the hardest to see where to go and what to do next can be a real pain. Also the enemies could have been done better. I kind of feel like they are more of a nuisance than anything else. THere is a swarm of tiny enemies for example that slows you down and makes you less mobile and is therefor generally your death. This of course also means that once it has you escaping gets even harder. What is even worse is that these are most commonly found in the already hard enough gravitation segments. The other 2 enemy types are less annoying but all together I think this game could have done without them. Oh and devs you will never read this but: PLEASE DEACTIVATE PAST CHECKPOINTS THAT NO SENSIBLE PERSON WOULD USE ANYMORE IN SOME PATCH! You can easyly lose everything in some sections of the game because instead of falling to your death you fall on top of a checkpoint hat is basically where you started half an hour ago and there is no way you can undo it and that is just rage inducing and a game killer. Thankfully it isnt possible for this to happen often and probably you just have to have my luck for it to happen at all. Now about speedrunning: yes, this game is used for speedrunners showing off with leaderboards etc. Is it hard to speedrun through? Is it good and fun to speedrun through? No idea, if there was an opposite of a speedrunner that'd be me. Though the game often offers paths that are faster but as a price more difficult. Now if you, like me, are not a speedrunner that isnt even an issue. How fast you complete the game means nothing if you dont want to shine on some leaderboard. Oh but dont excepect the game to be slow, until you reach a platform where nothing tries to kill you you have to be fast and precise or die. All together great fun but not very long, by on sale if you like challenges

title: DeadCore
text: Deadcore is a mesmerizing little game. This one totally slipped past my radar, and if it was not for the great Humble Bundles I would have taken even longer to experience it. To start out, this game is MADE for VR. When VR hits I totally hope we see more games like this because the idea of jumping around some tower in the sky and doing puzzles in an FPS environment is basically what a lot of people are going to go crazy over in the virtual realm. As for the game: it has stellar art direction, though the game was obviously made on a budget. I consistently felt like I was actually involved and trying to escape or find whatever the story was pointing me too. I felt like I existed in the virtual realm, and even though I'm only on a 42 inch the game made me feel like I was in a virtual reality prison I had to escape. The devs deserve their win for that alone. They also encourage you to explore the tower and its offshoots with varied pickups throughout and sound files as well some interesting tidbits on the story that are vague but intriguing. The level design is fairly masterful and you will always find yourself looking out to see what is around you and how to get there. The mechanics for jumping seem pretty straightforward to me and the momentum and actual controls felt good to me once I got ahold of how to use my DS4 in the game. I wasn't feeling too much lag at all. You can use a controller with Input Mapper and Xpadder--I use a DS4--or whatever other combination you want to try. Keyboard and mouse controls are fine too. Custome resolution with Nvidia does let 1080p users get 4K supersampling, but I could not get my sound to work properly. Otherwise I use base 1080p and inject SMAA and FXAA. Really wish this game was patched or updated for true controller support and 4K. In the end Deadcore slipped by a lot of people. And that is just too bad, because the platforming here is some of the best in 3D gaming. A remarkable game that I hope will someday find its way to more systems and definitely VR. In need of some polish for sure, but what's there is a fine game.

text: If Tron, Magrunner: Dark Pulse, and Portal had a charming, deformed baby, this would be it. Pretty sweet game, nice visuals and the platforming is addictive. The sound design is particularly cool. The "climbing a tower" concept that is imbued throughout the game and its various approaches you can use to get around its levels is refreshing. No plug and play USB controller support is kind of a bummer, but with the precision and speed needed to get through some levels a mouse would probably be favorable regardless. One minute you'll be frantically activating platforms and dodging laser platforms and the next you'll be gazing at sprawling vistas and the upcoming challenges.. It's a great game, particularly if you're into first person platforming ala Portal, Magrunner, etc, you should definitely give it a go.

title: Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten (DX edition)
text: This game, is awesome. It's a very refreshing aproach to the classic visualized RPG genre. It combines the best aspects of "Tower Defense" games and what's usually considered rpg-elements (even though I disagree on the common definition of what these are). The game itself doesn't give you much freedom of movement in general, you just kind of advance to one point of the story to the next, but that didn't actually bother me, surprisingly. One of the nicest aspects of the game is the option of giving every single one of the characters your group gets a name of your choice. There's always some dialog, main char asking "What's your name?" and you get a prompt asking you for a name, which is then used throughout the rest of the game (and can be changed if desired). The game puts you in the shoes of "The Librarian" (her name will be asked for first) who has the unique ability to summon her allies (regular fighters, archers mages and the like) into a "spirit realm" where the undead, which make up the bulk of the enemies encountered in the game, can be actually made re-dead for good. Therefore she's the one who needs to be tower-defended. The army of defenders consists of six different classes of units which can become six of each type (additional characters can just be recruited in towns for ingame scrap). They all level up and have skill that can be improved by the player with each levelup. The dialogues and the general story is actually quite good and really really funny, all the characters are quite sympathetic and just lovely insane. Also, the game has a neat turn when it comes to playing it a second time (new game+) because the second playthrough mode actually adds several new sidequest, an upgrade option for the unique weapons found during the first playthrough and a simply hilarious journal, which recieves entries every now and then as the journey progresses... extremely funny =D. Even though the game seems to be a finished release, I gather there's still people working on it, so it might even get additional content updates. Definitely recommended.

title: Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten (DX edition)
text: This is a great tower defense game with lots or RPG elements included.  Instead of towers, you have heroes you position along a path to defend your leader.  As these heroes fight, they level up and can be built into different styles of tower depending on the skills you take. Pros - Lots of good tower defense gameplay - Lots of well done RPG elements so you can modify each hero and personalize your play style - Good story and interesting characters - Lots of great items to equip to make your heroes (towers) even more effective - The game rewards replay of older levels on higher difficulties by giving your heroes (towers) more experience and the ability to unlock special items - Lots of replay value with all the difficulty levels and all the things that can be unlocked. - Challenging maps that sometimes require you to think outside your normal setups. Cons - Older graphics - Gameplay can be repetative if you're just interested in the story Overall this is a great game that I would highly recommend to an RPG or tower defense enthusiast. The game gives you the option of both relaxed gameplay and very challening maps if you want them.  (It also rewards your party for completing said maps.)

title: Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten (DX edition)
text: Defenders Quest is a well-balanced Tower Defense game that replaces static towers with RPG-element-laden characters. With six classes, skill trees and weapons and armor there's plenty of customization to be had. It is a little repetative, as the game expects you to run certain levels over a few times to gather much needed XP and money, but it doesn't overstay its welcome. It's got a story with characters I cared about, which is a hard thing to do for a TD game, and it ended before things started getting stale. A well-rounded experience! :) I would sing this game's praises in the same breath as Kingdom Rush. A gold standard to the genre.

title: Defense Grid: The Awakening
text: I have seldom played a better tower defense game. Set in a galaxy far, far away on a planet with a dormant defense grid.. You must defend military bases against aliens trying to steal your power cores as you re-activate the defense system. As usually the towers have different skills, but 1 tower does not overpower the others unlike in many others TDG's. You are forced to place your towers in different strategic series in connection with the other types and the map layout. Unlike if you place a SuperMonkey in Bloons TDG. You have to create a happy family, and everyone are equal in this time and age. :p.. No, I am your father! The 3D view is amazing, you can really think tactic with a zoom, turn and scroll function.< The rewind option is also great, while it doesn't make the game dead easy. Nice graphic, actually good detailed. High replay value - especially since there's a highscore system with your friends' results too. You can easily spend 100 hours beating this game! Many maps and game-modes - gives you quite a challenge, but a map is not impossible to beat, you just need to change your strategy from map to map. The DLC's are nice, to a fair price too. The game is cheap too, especially with how much time you can spend on it.  I can't find any negative things, except the feeling of frustration for when you just can't get a gold ranking, or when your friends beat your hardearned highscores. This game has little to do with Star Wars and the cake is a lie.

title: Defense Grid: The Awakening
text: Simple concept and easy to get into yet a challenge to perfect. Every level has multiple ways to succeed (& fail) which means even when you get your all your Gold medals you still can go back and play it completely differently. This is a rare trait to see in a game to have such good balanced mechanics (between real-time & strategic planning) and level design that it constantly feels fresh! Balance continues in the tower design & difficulty levels where it often feels like a real tug-of-war with the aliens. This and all the DLCs are exceptional fun, worth every $$$ and even going on 5 years since I purchased I still find this game a great experience. It is the definitive Tower Defense game with replayability not often seen in the modern world of disposable gaming. Cannot say a bad thing about the game other than it will consume your soul and spit out Rasberries!! - You'll keep coming back to play again and again. Graphically, it is feeling a little low-def in 2014, but does not detract from the experience. I would definitely say it's worth the standard price. It's a truly big game, packed with everything one could ask for in this genre.
